answer.reason: The two versions differ only when max_attempts is None. In that case `routes[:None]` returns every element in the same order, so the returned tuple is identical. For any other value, both versions run the same slice, so the result is the same no matter how many routes the plan has.
sources: A request shall never attempt more routes than the configured route-attempt limit.

review.reason: When options.max_attempts is None, the Python slice operation routes[:None] evaluates to a full copy of the list, resulting in the exact same output tuple as skipping the slice entirely. The function's observable behavior is identical in both versions.
